evidence_timeline.summary: EP261006a (AT 2026aetp, Gaia DR3 2587044864659595392) was first detected by the Einstein Probe at 2026-10-06T17:49:57 UTC ([GCN #45826](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45826)) and was subsequently suggested to be a possible TDE ([GCN #45831](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45831)). Subsequent spectroscopic observations revealed a clear blue continuum across the entire spectrum, with no prominent absorption or emission features ([GCN #45833](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45833)).

publication_revisions.abstract: EP261006a (AT 2026aetp, Gaia DR3 2587044864659595392) was first detected by the Einstein Probe at 2026-10-06T17:49:57 UTC ([GCN #45826](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45826)) and was subsequently suggested to be a possible TDE ([GCN #45831](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45831)). Subsequent spectroscopic observations revealed a clear blue continuum across the entire spectrum, with no prominent absorption or emission features ([GCN #45833](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45833)).
